approved: The majority voted against a [motion](https://www.openaustralia.org.au/senate/?gid=2024-03-21.7.16) to read the bill for a second time. In parliamentary jargon, they voted against agreeing with the main idea of the bill. This means the bill has been rejected and will not be considered any further in parliament. ### What does this bill do? According to the [bills homepage](https://www.aph.gov.au/Parliamentary_Business/Bills_Legislation/Bills_Search_Results/Result?bId=s1138), the bill: > *Establishes a legislative framework for a national plebiscite to be held in conjunction with the next general election that would ask Australians “Do you think the current rate of immigration to Australia is too high?”.*
Moved to suspend standing orders so the Plebiscite (Future Migration Level) Bill 2018 could be restored to the Notice Paper and considered at the second reading stage; the question was agreed to.

Moved the Plebiscite (Future Migration Level) Bill 2018, proposing a public vote on zero net migration for a period, arguing that lower migration would ease pressure on housing and infrastructure; the coalition said it would oppose the bill while supporting public input on sustainable migration levels.
